LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 LISTENING FOR INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for Information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for Information, part of Strand 1 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do get information from an oral text? 2. Why are some individuals considered community heroes or heroines?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

A. identify target words (names of people, things and place

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly with peers to pick out nouns (names of people, things and places) in a text,

2. list the nouns on charts for display in the language corner,

3. discuss with peers the various ways of listening for information,

4. listen to an audio recording on community heroes and heroines,

5. pick out the main ideas from the recording,

6. make notes on the qualities of an ethical leader from the text,

7. share their findings with peers for review,

8. work collaboratively to role-play a news report on a community hero or heroine of choice. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly with peers to pick out nouns (names of people, things and places) in a text,
2. list the nouns on charts for display in the language corner,
3. discuss with peers the various ways of listening for information,
4. listen to an audio recording on community heroes and heroines,
5. pick out the main ideas from the recording,
6. make notes on the qualities of an ethical leader from the text,
7. share their findings with peers for review,
8. work collaboratively to role-play a news report on a community hero or heroine of choice. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Listening for Information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner engages actively using facts and examples when

sharing their findings on qualities of an ethical leader with peers for review.

• Digital Literacy: It is enhanced as the learner interacts with digital content when listening to an audio recording on

community heroes and heroines.

Values:
• Respect: This is developed as the learner accommodates diverse opinions when discussing with peers the various ways of

listening for information.

• Responsibility: It is enhanced as the learner diligently takes up assigned roles when working with peers to roleplay a news

report on a community hero and heroine of choice.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Good Governance: The learner interacts with texts on community heroes and heroines and identifies the qualities of an ethical

leader.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate information derived from the texts on community heroes and heroines to the concept of nationalism in

Social Studies.
